metrics.conduction_pathway: SA Node (70–80 bpm) -> Internodal Tracts -> AV Node (0.1 s delay!) -> Bundle of His -> Left/Right Bundle Branches -> Purkinje Fibers (4 m/s)
metrics.sa_node_phases: Phase 4 (Slow Na+ 'funny' current If via HCN + T-type Ca2+) -> Phase 0 (L-type Ca2+ influx, NO fast Na+!) -> Phase 3 (K+ efflux)
metrics.ventricular_phases: Phase 0 (Fast Na+ influx) -> Phase 1 (Ito K+ notch) -> Phase 2 (250 ms Plateau: L-type Ca2+ in = K+ out!) -> Phase 3 (K+ out) -> Phase 4 (-90 mV)
metrics.cardiac_equations: Cardiac Output (CO) = Heart Rate (HR) × Stroke Volume (SV) | SV = EDV (120 mL) - ESV (50 mL) = 70 mL | Ejection Fraction = SV / EDV (~58%)

mechanism: **1. SA NODAL PACEMAKER POTENTIAL vs. VENTRICULAR MYOCYTE ACTION POTENTIAL**:

• **SA Node (Autorhythmic)**: Lacks a stable resting potential! Starts at $-60\ \text{mV}$ and spontaneously depolarizes during **Phase 4 (Pacemaker Prepotential)** via hyperpolarization-activated cyclic-nucleotide-gated **'Funny' $\text{Na}^+$ channels ($I_f$ / HCN4)** and **T-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels**. Once threshold ($-40\ \text{mV}$) is reached, **Phase 0 Upstroke is driven entirely by slow L-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels** (not fast $\text{Na}^+$!), followed by **Phase 3 $\text{K}^+$ repolarization**.

• **Ventricular Contractile Myocyte**: Stable resting potential at $-90\ \text{mV}$ (**Phase 4**). **Phase 0** = explosive fast voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ influx ($+20\ \text{mV}$); **Phase 1** = transient outward $\text{K}^+$ ($I_{to}$); **Phase 2 (200–300 ms Plateau)** = inward **L-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ influx** exactly balances outward delayed-rectifier **$\text{K}^+$ efflux** (this long refractory plateau **prevents cardiac tetany** so the ventricle has time to refill with blood before contracting again!).
**2. THE ELECTROCARDIOGRAM (ECG) & WIGGERS CARDIAC CYCLE**:
• **P Wave**: Atrial depolarization (precedes atrial systole; PR interval = $0.12\text{–}0.20\ \text{s}$ reflects AV nodal delay).

• **QRS Complex**: Ventricular depolarization (masks atrial repolarization; immediately precedes Isovolumetric Ventricular Contraction where AV valves [Mitral/Tricuspid] snap shut = **First Heart Sound S1 'Lub'**).
• **ST Segment**: Isoelectric plateau when the entire ventricular myocardium is depolarized (Phase 2).

• **T Wave**: Ventricular repolarization (followed by Isovolumetric Ventricular Relaxation where Semilunar valves [Aortic/Pulmonary] snap shut at the **Dicrotic Notch** = **Second Heart Sound S2 'Dub'**).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Cardiac Physiology & Autonomic Control:
• **How do Sympathetic (Norepinephrine) vs. Parasympathetic (Vagus Nerve / Acetylcholine) inputs alter the SA Node Pacemaker Slope?**

– **Sympathetic ($\beta_1$-Adrenergic Receptor $\rightarrow G_s \rightarrow \uparrow \text{cAMP}$)**: cAMP binds directly to **HCN4 ($I_f$) channels** and PKA phosphorylates L-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels, **steepening the Phase 4 pacemaker slope** so threshold is reached faster (**Positive Chronotropic Effect** = $\uparrow$ HR) and increasing $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ contractility (**Positive Inotropic Effect**).

– **Parasympathetic ($\text{M}_2$ Muscarinic Receptor $\rightarrow G_i$)** : The **$G_{\beta\gamma}$ subunit** directly opens **GIRK ($I_{\text{KACh}}$) $\text{K}^+$ channels** (hyperpolarizing the SA node to $-75\ \text{mV}$) while $G_{i\alpha}$ lowers cAMP (**flattening the Phase 4 slope** = **Negative Chronotropic Effect**).

• **Frank–Starling Law of the Heart**: Within physiological limits, increasing venous return (**End-Diastolic Volume / Preload**) stretches ventricular sarcomeres closer to their optimal overlap length ($\sim 2.2\ \mu\text{m}$) and increases Troponin C $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ sensitivity, automatically increasing **Stroke Volume** to match venous return!
• **Valvular Closure Landmarks**:
– **Isovolumetric Contraction**: Occurs between **AV valve closure (S1)** and **Semilunar valve opening** (ALL 4 valves are closed; volume is constant while pressure skyrockets!).
– **Isovolumetric Relaxation**: Occurs between **Semilunar valve closure (S2)** and **AV valve opening** (ALL 4 valves are closed!).
pathology: **Long QT Syndrome (Romano-Ward / Jervell & Lange-Nielsen)** & **AV Heart Blocks**:

• Loss-of-function mutations in cardiac delayed-rectifier $\text{K}^+$ channels (*KCNQ1* or *KCNH2* / hERG) prolong Phase 2/3 repolarization, lengthening the **QT interval** on the ECG and predisposing patients to lethal *Torsades de Pointes* ventricular fibrillation.

• **Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)**: Acute coronary occlusion causes **ST-Segment Elevation** and pathological Q waves on the ECG alongside serum elevation of **Cardiac Troponin I / T (cTnI/cTnT)** and **CK-MB**.
lab_workbench: Einthoven's Triangle Bipolar Limb Lead Recording (Leads I, II, III): **Einthoven's Law** states that at any given instant in the cardiac cycle, the electrical potential of **Lead II equals the sum of Lead I plus Lead III** ($\text{II} = \text{I} + \text{III}$, where Lead I = LA – RA, Lead II = LL – RA, and Lead III = LL – LA).

metrics.hb_vs_mb_kinetics: Myoglobin (Monomer, Hyperbolic curve, P50 ≈ 2.8 mmHg, nH = 1.0) vs. Hemoglobin A (α2β2 Tetramer, Sigmoidal curve, P50 ≈ 26 mmHg, nH ≈ 2.8)
metrics.right_shift_unloading: Caused by ↑ PCO2, ↓ pH (↑ H+ = Bohr Effect), ↑ Temperature, and ↑ 2,3-BPG (Increases P50 -> Decreases O2 affinity -> Unloads O2 to tissues!)
metrics.co2_transport_forms: 70% as Plasma Bicarbonate (HCO3- via RBC Carbonic Anhydrase II) + 23% as Carbaminohemoglobin (Hb-NH-COO-) + 7% Dissolved CO2
metrics.chloride_shift_hamburger: In tissues: HCO3- exits RBC in strict 1:1 electroneutral exchange for Cl- entering via Band-3 (AE1 / SLC4A1) anion exchanger!

mechanism: **1. PERUTZ'S T-TO-R ALLOSTERIC SWITCH IN HEMOGLOBIN ($\alpha_2\beta_2$)**:

• **Deoxyhemoglobin (T-State = 'Tense', Low $\text{O}_2$ Affinity)**: Stabilized by a network of inter-subunit **salt bridges** (including **His-146** on the $\beta$-chains) and by one molecule of negatively charged **2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG)** sitting inside the central positively charged cavity (lined by His-143, Lys-82, and N-termini of the two $\beta$-chains). In the T-state, the high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ion is pulled **0.4–0.6 Å out of the porphyrin plane** toward the proximal **Histidine F8 (His-92)**.

• **Oxyhemoglobin (R-State = 'Relaxed', 150x Higher $\text{O}_2$ Affinity)**: Binding of $\text{O}_2$ to the first heme converts $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to a smaller low-spin state that **snaps flat into the porphyrin plane**, pulling the proximal **His-F8** and the F-helix with it! This ruptures the inter-subunit salt bridges, expels 2,3-BPG, and rotates the $\alpha_1\beta_1$ dimer $15^\circ$ relative to $\alpha_2\beta_2$ into the high-affinity **R-state** (**Positive Cooperativity**, Hill coefficient $n_H \approx 2.8$).
**2. THE BOHR EFFECT (In Metabolically Active Tissues) vs. HALDANE EFFECT (In Lungs)**:

• **Bohr Effect**: Metabolizing tissues produce $\text{CO}_2$ and Lactic acid ($\downarrow \text{pH}$). Protons ($\text{H}^+$) protonate **His-146** on $\beta$-globin (enabling it to form a stabilizing salt bridge with Asp-94 in the **T-state**), while $\text{CO}_2$ reacts with N-terminal amino groups to form negatively charged **Carbaminohemoglobin ($\text{Hb-NH-COO}^-$)**—shifting the dissociation curve to the **RIGHT ($\uparrow P_{50}$)** to dump extra $\text{O}_2$ precisely where tissues need it most!

• **Haldane Effect**: In the lungs, binding of high $\text{O}_2$ converts Hb into the **R-state**, which is a stronger acid (releases $\text{H}^+$ from His-146 to drive $\text{H}^+ + \text{HCO}_3^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$) and has lower affinity for carbamino-$\text{CO}_2$—**promoting $\text{CO}_2$ unloading in the alveoli**!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Fetal Hemoglobin, High Altitude & CO Poisoning:

• **Why does Fetal Hemoglobin ($\text{HbF}, \alpha_2\gamma_2$) have a HIGHER affinity for $\text{O}_2$ ($P_{50} \approx 19\ \text{mmHg}$, Left-Shifted curve) than Maternal Adult Hemoglobin ($\text{HbA}, \alpha_2\beta_2, P_{50} \approx 26\ \text{mmHg}$)?** Because in the fetal **$\gamma$-globin chain**, the positively charged **Histidine-143** of the adult $\beta$-chain is replaced by an uncharged **Serine (Ser-143)**! With two fewer positive charges in the central cavity, **HbF binds 2,3-BPG much more weakly**, spending more time in the high-affinity R-state so it can extract $\text{O}_2$ across the placenta from maternal HbA!

• **High-Altitude Acclimatization**: Hypoxia increases RBC glycolysis and activates **BPG Mutase**, elevating RBC **[2,3-BPG]** within 24–48 hours $\rightarrow$ shifts the curve to the **RIGHT ($\uparrow P_{50}$)** to maintain tissue $\text{O}_2$ unloading despite lower arterial $P_{\text{O}_2}$! *(Long-term: renal peritubular interstitial cells stabilize **HIF-1$\alpha$** to secrete **Erythropoietin [EPO]**).

• **Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning Double Whammy**: CO binds $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ with ~220x higher affinity than $\text{O}_2$ (reducing total $\text{O}_2$-carrying capacity by 50% at 50% HbCO), **AND locking 1 or 2 CO molecules onto an Hb tetramer traps the remaining subunits in the high-affinity R-state**—shifting the curve to the **LEFT** (converting it from sigmoidal to hyperbolic!) so the remaining bound $\text{O}_2$ **cannot be unloaded** to starving brain/heart tissues!
pathology: **Sickle Cell Anemia ($\text{HbS}$)**: Point mutation (**Glu6Val**) on the $\beta$-globin surface creates a sticky hydrophobic patch specifically in the **Deoxy (T-state)** that polymerizes into rigid fibers (treated clinically with **Hydroxyurea**, which reactivates fetal **$\text{HbF } (\alpha_2\gamma_2)$** expression to block HbS polymerization!).

**Methemoglobinemia ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$)**: Nitrites or oxidative drugs oxidize heme $\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}$ (**Methemoglobin**, which **cannot bind $\text{O}_2$** and turns blood chocolate-brown); normally reduced back to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ by RBC **NADH-Cytochrome $b_5$ Reductase** (or treated clinically with **Methylene Blue**).
lab_workbench: Hill Plot Linearization ($\log[Y / (1 - Y)] \text{ vs. } \log P_{\text{O}_2}$): Myoglobin yields a straight line with slope **$n_H = 1.0$** across all $P_{\text{O}_2}$; Hemoglobin yields an asymptote of slope $1.0$ at extreme low/high $P_{\text{O}_2}$ (when all 4 subunits are in T or R) and a maximum central slope of **$n_H \approx 2.8\text{–}3.0$** around $P_{50}$.

node_glomerular_clearance.title: Glomerular Filtration (GFR), Starling Forces & Renal Clearance Math
node_glomerular_clearance.subtitle: Fenestrated Endothelium + GBM + Podocyte Slit Diaphragm | Inulin vs. PAH Clearance Equations

metrics.net_filtration_pressure: NFP = P_GC (55 mmHg) - P_BS (15 mmHg) - π_GC (30 mmHg) = +10 mmHg | GFR = Kf × NFP ≈ 125 mL/min (180 L/day!)
metrics.clearance_equation: C_x = (U_x × V) / P_x [mL/min] | Filtered Load = GFR × P_x | Excretion Rate = U_x × V
metrics.gold_standard_markers: Inulin (or Creatinine) Clearance = GFR (125 mL/min) | PAH Clearance = Effective Renal Plasma Flow (ERPF ≈ 625 mL/min)
metrics.filtration_fraction: FF = GFR / RPF = 125 / 625 = 0.20 (20% of renal plasma is filtered at the glomerulus)

mechanism: **1. THE THREE-LAYER GLOMERULAR FILTRATION BARRIER (Size- AND Charge-Selective!)**:
• **Layer 1**: Fenestrated glomerular capillary endothelium (70–100 nm pores; excludes blood cells).
• **Layer 2**: **Glomerular Basement Membrane (GBM)**—meshwork of **Type IV Collagen** and negatively charged **Heparan Sulfate proteoglycans**.
• **Layer 3**: Visceral epithelial **Podocyte foot processes** bridged by a 40 nm **Slit Diaphragm** (**Nephrin + Podocin**).

*Charge Selectivity Rule*: Because the GBM and podocyte sialoproteins are rich in **negative charges**, negatively charged plasma **Albumin** (~66 kDa, radius 3.6 nm) is electrostatically **repelled** and excluded from the filtrate (<0.02% filtered), whereas neutral dextrans of the exact same 3.6 nm size pass through easily!
**2. OPPOSITE EFFECTS OF AFFERENT vs. EFFERENT ARTERIOLAR CONSTRICTION**:

• **Afferent Arteriole Constriction** (e.g., high sympathetic tone / NSAIDs blocking prostaglandins): Drops glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure ($P_{\text{GC}}$) $\rightarrow$ **Decreases BOTH RPF and GFR**.

• **Mild-to-Moderate Efferent Arteriole Constriction** (mediated specifically by **Angiotensin II**!): Backs up blood inside the glomerulus, **increasing $P_{\text{GC}}$** while decreasing RPF $\rightarrow$ **Increases GFR (or maintains GFR during renal hypoperfusion) and INCREASES Filtration Fraction ($	ext{FF} = \text{GFR}/\text{RPF}$)**!
csir_high_yield: Renal Clearance Numerical Rules (Guaranteed CSIR NET Part C Calculation Problem!):
Always start with two formulas: **$\text{Clearance } (C_x) = \frac{U_x \times V}{P_x}$** and **$\text{Filtered Load} = \text{GFR} \times P_x$**:
• **If $C_x = C_{\text{Inulin}}$ ($125\ \text{mL/min}$)**: Substance $X$ is freely filtered and experiences **zero net reabsorption or secretion** (e.g., **Inulin**).

• **If $C_x < C_{\text{Inulin}}$ (or $\text{Excreted } U_x V < \text{Filtered Load } \text{GFR} \times P_x$)**: Substance $X$ undergoes **NET TUBULAR REABSORPTION**! (e.g., **Glucose** at normal plasma levels $<180\ \text{mg/dL}$ is 100% reabsorbed in the PCT via **SGLT2/SGLT1**, so **$C_{\text{Glucose}} = 0\ \text{mL/min}$**; **Urea** has $C_{\text{Urea}} \approx 65\ \text{mL/min}$).

• **If $C_x > C_{\text{Inulin}}$ (or $\text{Excreted } U_x V > \text{Filtered Load } \text{GFR} \times P_x$)**: Substance $X$ undergoes **NET TUBULAR SECRETION**! (e.g., **PAH [Para-aminohippuric acid]** is filtered AND 100% secreted by peritubular OAT transporters in a single pass, so **$C_{\text{PAH}} = \text{ERPF} \approx 625\ \text{mL/min}$**; Penicillin and $\text{H}^+$ also have $C_x > \text{GFR}$).
pathology: **Minimal Change Disease / Nephrotic Syndrome**: Loss of negative heparan sulfate charges on the GBM (or mutations in *NPHS1* [**Nephrin**] in congenital nephrotic syndrome) allows massive filtration of negatively charged **Albumin** into the urine (**Proteinuria $>3.5\ \text{g/day}$**), dropping plasma oncotic pressure ($\pi_{\text{GC}}$) and causing generalized **pitting edema**!

**SGLT2 Inhibitors (Dapagliflozin / Empagliflozin)**: Block proximal tubule $\text{Na}^+$/Glucose cotransporter 2 to lower the renal threshold for glucose and excrete excess blood glucose in Type 2 Diabetes.
lab_workbench: Glucose Titration Curve (Renal Transport Maximum $T_m$ & 'Splay'): Below plasma $[\text{Glucose}] = 180\ \text{mg/dL}$ (Renal Threshold), 100% of filtered glucose is reabsorbed; above $300\ \text{mg/dL}$, all SGLT2/SGLT1 carriers saturate at **$T_m = 375\ \text{mg/min}$**, and the excretion curve parallels the filtered load curve.

node_countercurrent_nephron.title: The Nephron Countercurrent Multiplier (Loop of Henle), RAAS & ADH Aquaporin-2
node_countercurrent_nephron.subtitle: 300 to 1,200 mOsm/L Medullary Gradient | Thin Descending (H2O) vs. Thick Ascending NKCC2 (Diluting Segment)

metrics.pct_reabsorption: Iso-osmotic (300 mOsm/L)! Reabsorbs 67% of filtered Na+ & H2O + 100% of Glucose & Amino Acids + 85% of HCO3-
metrics.thin_descending_limb: Freely permeable to H2O (via Aquaporin-1); impermeable to NaCl -> Tubular fluid concentrates to 1,200 mOsm/L at hairpin turn!
metrics.thick_ascending_limb: 'Diluting Segment'! 100% IMPERMEABLE to H2O; actively pumps out Na+-K+-2Cl- via NKCC2 -> Fluid becomes HYPO-OSMOTIC (~100 mOsm/L)!
metrics.collecting_duct_adh: Principal Cells: ADH (V2 Receptor -> cAMP/PKA) inserts Aquaporin-2 (AQP2) into apical membrane + Urea recycling builds 1,200 mOsm/L papilla!

mechanism: **1. HOW JUXTAMEDULLARY NEPHRONS BUILD THE 300 $\rightarrow$ 1,200 mOsm/L MEDULLARY GRADIENT**:

• **The 'Single Effect' (Thick Ascending Limb / TAL)**: Epithelial cells of the Thick Ascending Limb are **completely impermeable to water** (lack aquaporins) and use the apical **NKCC2 ($\text{Na}^+\text{-K}^+\text{-2Cl}^-$) cotransporter** to pump $\text{NaCl}$ out of the lumen into the medullary interstitium—generating a $200\ \text{mOsm/L}$ horizontal gradient while leaving the tubular fluid exiting the Loop of Henle **hypo-osmotic ($\sim 100\ \text{mOsm/L}$, the 'Diluting Segment')**!

• **Countercurrent Multiplication**: Because the **Thin Descending Limb** is freely permeable to water (**AQP1**), water is osmotically drawn out into the hypertonic interstitium, concentrating descending tubular fluid to $1,200\ \text{mOsm/L}$ at the hairpin tip. Meanwhile, **Inner Medullary Urea Recycling** ( accounts for **~50% [$600\ \text{mOsm/L}$] of deep medullary osmolarity** via ADH-activated **UT-A1/A3** urea transporters) and hairpin **Vasa Recta Countercurrent Exchangers** (which prevent blood flow from washing away the medullary salt/urea gradient!) lock the $1,200\ \text{mOsm/L}$ gradient in place.
**2. THE RENIN–ANGIOTENSIN–ALDOSTERONE SYSTEM (RAAS) & ADH**:

• Low blood pressure / low macula densa $\text{NaCl}$ delivery $\rightarrow$ Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells secrete **Renin** (aspartyl protease) $\rightarrow$ cleaves liver **Angiotensinogen** into decapeptide **Angiotensin I (10 aa)** $\rightarrow$ pulmonary endothelial **ACE (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme)** cleaves it into octapeptide **Angiotensin II (8 aa)**.

• **Angiotensin II**: Constricts arterioles (efferent > afferent), stimulates PCT $\text{Na}^+/\text{H}^+$ exchange, stimulates hypothalamic **ADH** release & thirst, and stimulates the **Zona Glomerulosa** of the adrenal cortex to secrete **Aldosterone** (which upregulates **ENaC** $\text{Na}^+$ channels and $\text{ROMK}$ $\text{K}^+$ channels in **Principal Cells** of the Late DCT/Collecting Duct!).
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Tubular Segment Osmolarity & Diuretic Matching Questions:

• **In which segment of the nephron is tubular fluid ALWAYS HYPO-OSMOTIC (~100 mOsm/L) relative to plasma, regardless of whether ADH is maximal or zero?** Entering the **Early Distal Convoluted Tubule (just exiting the Thick Ascending Limb)**! Why? Because the Thick Ascending Limb actively pumps out $\text{NaCl}$ via NKCC2 while being 100% impermeable to water!

• **Where is the highest percentage of filtered water reabsorbed when ADH is ABSENT vs. PRESENT?** In **BOTH cases**, the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)** reabsorbs the largest absolute volume and percentage (~67%) of filtered water obligatorily! **ADH (Vasopressin)** only controls the facultative final 10–15% of water reabsorption in the **Collecting Duct** (by triggering exocytic insertion of **Aquaporin-2 [AQP2]** vesicles into the apical membrane via **$V_2 \text{ GPCR} \rightarrow G_s \rightarrow \text{cAMP} \rightarrow \text{PKA}$**).
• **Site-Specific Diuretic Pharmacology**:
– **Acetazolamide**: Inhibits **Carbonic Anhydrase** in the **PCT**.

– **Furosemide (Loop Diuretic)**: Inhibits **NKCC2 ($\text{Na}^+\text{-K}^+\text{-2Cl}^-$)** in the **Thick Ascending Limb** (washout of medullary gradient + causes $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ excretion because it abolishes the lumen-positive potential generated by ROMK!).
– **Thiazide Diuretics**: Inhibit **NCC ($\text{Na}^+\text{-Cl}^-$ cotransporter)** in the **Early DCT** (uniquely *increases* $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ reabsorption!).
– **Spironolactone (Aldosterone antagonist) & Amiloride (ENaC blocker)**: Act on **Principal Cells of Collecting Duct** (**$\text{K}^+$-Sparing Diuretics**!).
pathology: • **Central DI**: Failure of posterior pituitary to secrete ADH $\rightarrow$ massive excretion ($>10\ \text{L/day}$) of ultra-dilute urine ($50\ \text{mOsm/L}$); **100% rescued by intranasal Desmopressin (dDAVP)**.

• **Nephrogenic DI**: Mutations in the renal **$V_2$ Receptor (*AVPR2*, X-linked)** or **Aquaporin-2 (*AQP2*)** (or **Lithium** therapy inhibiting cAMP) $\rightarrow$ collecting duct fails to respond to ADH (**NOT rescued by Desmopressin**!).

**Bartter Syndrome** (loss of NKCC2 in TAL; mimics Furosemide) vs. **Gitelman Syndrome** (loss of NCC in DCT; mimics Thiazides) vs. **Liddle Syndrome** (gain-of-function mutation deleting the PY Nedd4-2 ubiquitin-ligase degron on **ENaC**, causing severe hypertension + hypokalemia with *low* renin/aldosterone!).
lab_workbench: Free-Water Clearance ($C_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = V - C_{\text{osm}} = V - \frac{U_{\text{osm}} V}{P_{\text{osm}}}$): When urine is dilute ($U_{\text{osm}} < P_{\text{osm}}$, low ADH), **$C_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$ is POSITIVE** (solute-free water is being excreted); when urine is concentrated ($U_{\text{osm}} > P_{\text{osm}}$, high ADH), **$C_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$ is NEGATIVE** (designated **$T^c_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$**, solute-free water is being reabsorbed into blood).

mechanism: **1. HYPOTHALAMIC–PITUITARY PORTAL vs. NEUROSECRETORY AXES**:

• **Posterior Pituitary (Neurohypophysis)**: Magnocellular neurons in the **Supraoptic Nucleus (SON, mainly ADH)** and **Paraventricular Nucleus (PVN, mainly Oxytocin)** synthesize preprohormones packaged with **Neurophysin I (Oxytocin) or Neurophysin II (ADH)** and transport them down axons through the infundibular stalk to release directly into systemic capillaries.
• **Anterior Pituitary (Adenohypophysis)**: Regulated via the **Hypothalamo-Hypophyseal Portal System**:
– **TRH (Tripeptide: pGlu-His-Pro-NH2)** $\rightarrow$ Thyrotrophs $\rightarrow$ **TSH** (and Prolactin!).
– **CRH** $\rightarrow$ Corticotrophs (**POMC** precursor cleaved into **ACTH** + **$\alpha$-MSH** + **$\beta$-Endorphin**) $\rightarrow$ **Cortisol**.

– **GnRH (Pulsatile!)** $\rightarrow$ Gonadotrophs $\rightarrow$ **FSH & LH** (*Note*: **Continuous non-pulsatile GnRH agonist infusion [Leuprolide] downregulates pituitary GnRH receptors and SHUTS DOWN FSH/LH!**).

node_action_potential_hodgkin.subtitle: Fast m-Gate Activation vs. Slow h-Gate Ball-and-Chain Inactivation (Absolute Refractory Period)

metrics.equilibrium_potentials: E_K ≈ -90 mV | E_Cl ≈ -70 mV | E_Na ≈ +60 mV | E_Ca ≈ +125 mV | Neuronal Resting V_m ≈ -70 mV (set by K+ leak channels + Na+/K+ ATPase)
metrics.nernst_equation_37c: E_ion = (61.5 / z) × log10( [Ion]_out / [Ion]_in ) [in mV at 37°C; 58 mV at 20°C]
metrics.na_channel_gates: 2 Gates: Fast Activation Gate (m-gate) + Slow Inactivation 'Ball-and-Chain' Gate (h-gate)! K+ channel has ONLY 1 Slow Gate (n-gate)
metrics.refractory_periods: Absolute Refractory Period = Na+ h-gates are INACTIVATED (0% excitability) | Relative Refractory Period = High K+ conductance g_K (hyperpolarized)

mechanism: **1. NERNST vs. GOLDMAN–HODGKIN–KATZ (GHK) VOLTAGE EQUATION**:

At rest ($V_m = -70\ \text{mV}$), membrane permeability is dominated by two-pore **$\text{K}^+$ leak channels** ($P_{\text{K}} : P_{\text{Na}} : P_{\text{Cl}} = 1.0 : 0.04 : 0.45$). Because $P_{\text{K}}$ is 25x higher than $P_{\text{Na}}$, resting $V_m$ sits close to $E_{\text{K}}$ ($-90\ \text{mV}$), while the electrogenic **$\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$-ATPase ($3\text{Na}^+ \text{ out} : 2\text{K}^+ \text{ in}$)** maintains the concentration gradients (contributing ~$-4\ \text{mV}$ directly).
**2. HODGKIN & HUXLEY GATING MECHANICS OF THE ACTION POTENTIAL**:

• **Resting State ($-70\ \text{mV}$)**: Voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ channel **Activation gate ($m$) is CLOSED**, while its cytoplasmic **Inactivation gate ($h$) is OPEN**. Voltage-gated $\text{K}^+$ channel gate ($n$) is **CLOSED**.

• **Threshold ($-55\ \text{mV}$) & Rising Phase Depolarization (Overshoot to $+35\ \text{mV}$)**: S4 voltage-sensor helices (rich in positively charged **Arginine/Lysine** every 3rd residue) slide outward, snapping the **fast $\text{Na}^+$ Activation gate ($m$) OPEN** ($P_{\text{Na}}/P_{\text{K}}$ flips to $20 : 1$, driving $V_m$ toward $E_{\text{Na}} = +60\ \text{mV}$ in a Hodgkin cycle).

• **Peak & Falling Phase Repolarization**: Within $0.5\text{–}1.0\ \text{ms}$, two events terminate the spike: (1) the delayed **$\text{Na}^+$ Inactivation gate ($h$, cytoplasmic III–IV linker loop) plugs the inner pore**, halting $\text{Na}^+$ influx, and (2) the slow **delayed-rectifier $\text{K}^+$ gate ($n$) opens**, driving massive $\text{K}^+$ efflux and an **After-Hyperpolarization (Undershoot)** toward $E_{\text{K}}$ ($-90\ \text{mV}$)!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Refractory Periods, Extracellular $\text{K}^+$ & Myelination:

• **What is the exact molecular basis of the ABSOLUTE Refractory Period (and why do action potentials propagate strictly unidirectionally from axon hillock to terminal)?** Because voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ channels enter the **INACTIVATED state ($h$-gate closed)** at the peak of the action potential! **An inactivated $\text{Na}^+$ channel CANNOT be reopened by any depolarizing stimulus, no matter how strong, until the membrane first REPOLARIZES back toward $-70\ \text{mV}$ to reset the $h$-gate!**

• **What happens to Resting Membrane Potential and Action Potential Peak if Extracellular $[\text{K}^+]_{\text{out}}$ is increased from $4\ \text{mM}$ to $20\ \text{mM}$ (Hyperkalemia)?** By the Nernst equation ($E_{\text{K}} = 61.5 \log([\text{K}^+]_{\text{out}}/[\text{K}^+]_{\text{in}})$), raising $[\text{K}^+]_{\text{out}}$ makes $E_{\text{K}}$ **LESS NEGATIVE (depolarizes the resting membrane potential!)**, whereas changing $[\text{Na}^+]_{\text{out}}$ alters the **peak overshoot height** of the action potential with minimal effect on resting $V_m$! *(Note: Severe chronic depolarization by hyperkalemia locks $\text{Na}^+$ $h$-gates in the inactivated state, causing **accommodation / flaccid paralysis and cardiac arrest in diastole**!).*

• **Cable Theory & Saltatory Conduction**: Conduction velocity increases with: (1) **Larger axon diameter ($a$)** (decreases internal axial resistance $r_i \propto 1/a^2$, hence the $1\ \text{mm}$ **Squid Giant Axon**!), and (2) **Myelination** (Oligodendrocytes in CNS; Schwann cells in PNS), which vastly **increases membrane resistance ($r_m$) and DECREASES membrane capacitance ($C_m$)**, increasing the **Length Constant ($\lambda = \sqrt{r_m / r_i}$)** so current leaps passively between **Nodes of Ranvier** (where $\text{Na}_v1.6$ channels are packed at $10,000/\mu\text{m}^2$)!
pathology: **Multiple Sclerosis (MS)** (CNS autoimmune demyelination) & **Guillain-Barré Syndrome** (PNS demyelination): Loss of myelin drops membrane resistance ($r_m$) and increases capacitance ($C_m$); current leaks out across the bare internodal membrane (which has almost zero voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ channels!), causing **conduction block** before reaching the next Node of Ranvier.
lab_workbench: Neher & Sakmann Patch-Clamp Configurations (1991 Nobel Prize) & Pronase Treatment: Applying **Pronase** (protease) to the **INSIDE (cytoplasmic face)** of a squid giant axon digests the III–IV linker loop (**$h$-gate**), completely **abolishing $\text{Na}^+$ channel inactivation** so $\text{Na}^+$ current stays open indefinitely during a voltage-clamp step!

mechanism: **1. PRESYNAPTIC VESICLE DOCKING & $\text{Ca}^{2+}$-TRIGGERED EXOCYTOSIS (Südhof / Rothman / Schekman)**:

• Neurotransmitters are pumped into synaptic vesicles by vesicular antiporters driven by a **V-type $\text{H}^+$-ATPase**. At the active zone, the vesicle **v-SNARE Synaptobrevin (VAMP)** partially zippers into a tight 4-helix bundle with the plasma-membrane **t-SNAREs Syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25** (clamped by Complexin and chaperoned by Munc18).

• Arrival of an action potential opens presynaptic **Voltage-Gated P/Q- and N-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ Channels ($\text{Ca}_v2.1/2.2$)**. Local $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ($>10\ \mu\text{M}$) binds the C2A/C2B domains of the vesicular $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ sensor **Synaptotagmin-1**, driving sub-millisecond membrane fusion and quantal neurotransmitter release (followed by **NSF + $\alpha$-SNAP** ATPase disassembly of cis-SNARE complexes for clathrin/dynamin recycling).
**2. HIPPOCAMPAL LONG-TERM POTENTIATION (LTP — Synaptic Plasticity & Memory)**:

• At resting membrane potential ($-70\ \text{mV}$), postsynaptic **NMDA Glutamate Receptors** are physically plugged inside their pore by an extracellular **$\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion**—even when Glutamate is bound! Only **AMPA Receptors** pass $\text{Na}^+$.

• High-frequency tetanic stimulation causes strong postsynaptic depolarization via AMPA receptors, which **electrostatically expels the $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ plug from the NMDA receptor** (**Coincidence Detector**: requires *both* presynaptic Glutamate AND postsynaptic depolarization!). Resulting **$\text{Ca}^{2+}$ influx through NMDA receptors** activates **CaMKII**, which phosphorylates AMPA receptors and inserts extra AMPA receptors into the postsynaptic density!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Clostridial Neurotoxins, NMJ Diseases & KCC2 Chloride Switch:
• **Botulinum Toxin (BoNT A–G) vs. Tetanus Toxin (TeNT) — Same Molecular Target, Opposite Clinical Paralysis!**:

– Both are $\text{Zn}^{2+}$-endopeptidases that cleave **SNARE proteins** (**BoNT-B and Tetanus toxin both cleave Synaptobrevin/VAMP at the exact same peptide bond**; BoNT-A/E cleave **SNAP-25**; BoNT-C cleaves **Syntaxin-1**).
– **Botulinum Toxin**: Acts peripherally at the **Cholinergic Neuromuscular Junction (NMJ)**, blocking **Acetylcholine** release $\rightarrow$ **FLACCID PARALYSIS**!

– **Tetanus Toxin (Tetanospasmin)**: Undergoes retrograde axonal transport (via cytoplasmic dynein!) up motor axons to **Renshaw Inhibitory Interneurons in the Spinal Cord**, blocking **Glycine and GABA** release $\rightarrow$ unchecked motor neuron firing $\rightarrow$ **SPASTIC PARALYSIS ('Lockjaw')**! (*Strychnine* causes identical spastic convulsions by competitively blocking postsynaptic **Glycine receptors**!).
• **Myasthenia Gravis vs. Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS)**:

– **Myasthenia Gravis**: Autoantibodies against **Postsynaptic Nicotinic ACh Receptors (nAChR)**; weakness **worsens** with repetitive muscle use; treated with **AChE inhibitors (Pyridostigmine / Neostigmine / Edrophonium)**.

– **Lambert-Eaton Syndrome**: Autoantibodies against **Presynaptic Voltage-Gated $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ Channels ($\text{Ca}_v2.1$)**; muscle strength paradoxically **improves** after brief repetitive high-frequency exercise as presynaptic $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ builds up!

• **Why is GABA Excitatory (Depolarizing) in Embryonic/Neonatal Neurons, but Inhibitory (Hyperpolarizing) in Mature Adult Neurons?** Embryonic neurons express high **NKCC1** (pumps $\text{Cl}^-$ *into* the cell, so intracellular $[\text{Cl}^-]$ is high and $E_{\text{Cl}} \approx -40\ \text{mV}$ $\rightarrow$ opening $\text{GABA}_A$ causes $\text{Cl}^-$ *efflux* and depolarization!). During postnatal maturation, neurons upregulate **KCC2** (extrudes $\text{Cl}^-$ *out* of the cell, dropping $E_{\text{Cl}}$ to $-75\ \text{mV}$ $\rightarrow$ opening $\text{GABA}_A$ causes $\text{Cl}^-$ *influx* and hyperpolarizing inhibition!).
pathology: **Organophosphate Nerve Agents (Sarin, Parathion, Malathion)**: Irreversibly phosphorylate the catalytic Serine of **Acetylcholinesterase (AChE)**, causing cholinergic crisis and respiratory muscle paralysis (treated with **Atropine** [muscarinic antagonist] + **Pralidoxime [2-PAM]**, which regenerates phosphorylated AChE before 'aging' occurs).

node_sensory_phototransduction.subtitle: 11-cis-Retinal Photoisomerization -> Rhodopsin -> Transducin -> PDE6 Hydrolyzes cGMP -> CNG Na+/Ca2+ Channels CLOSE!

metrics.dark_state_rod: High [cGMP] keeps Cyclic-Nucleotide-Gated (CNG) Na+/Ca2+ channels OPEN ('Dark Current') -> Rod is DEPOLARIZED (-40 mV) & Continuously Releases Glutamate!
metrics.light_cascade: Photon -> 11-cis to All-trans-Retinal -> Metarhodopsin II -> Transducin (Gtα-GTP) -> Activates cGMP Phosphodiesterase (PDE6) -> [cGMP] drops!
metrics.light_response_sign: CNG Na+/Ca2+ channels CLOSE -> Rod HYPERPOLARIZES (to -70 mV) -> Stops releasing Glutamate!

mechanism: Vertebrate Rod and Cone photoreceptors are famous because **Light HYPERPOLARIZES the cell** (the exact opposite of almost all other sensory receptors!):

1. **IN COMPLETE DARKNESS (The 'Dark Current')**: Rod outer-segment **Guanylyl Cyclase** continuously synthesizes **cGMP**. High cytosolic $[\text{cGMP}]$ binds and holds **Cyclic-Nucleotide-Gated (CNG) $\text{Na}^+/\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels OPEN**, allowing an inward 'Dark Current' of $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ that keeps the photoreceptor **DEPOLARIZED at $-40\ \text{mV}$**, continuously releasing **Glutamate** onto bipolar cells!
2. **IN LIGHT (Hyperpolarization Cascade)**:

• A single photon isomerizes **11-*cis*-retinal** (covalently bound via a protonated Schiff base to **Lys-296** of **Opsin**) into **All-*trans*-retinal**, converting Rhodopsin into active **Metarhodopsin II ($R^*$)**.
• $R^*$ activates the heterotrimeric G-protein **Transducin ($G_t$)** ($G_{t\alpha}\text{-GDP} \rightarrow G_{t\alpha}\text{-GTP}$).

• $G_{t\alpha}\text{-GTP}$ binds the inhibitory $\gamma$-subunits of **cGMP Phosphodiesterase (PDE6)**, unleashing PDE6 catalytic $\alpha\beta$ subunits to rapidly **hydrolyze cGMP into linear 5'-GMP**.
• Dropping $[\text{cGMP}]$ causes **CNG $\text{Na}^+/\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels to SNAP SHUT**, **HYPERPOLARIZING** the rod membrane to $-70\ \text{mV}$ and **halting Glutamate release**!

3. **LIGHT ADAPTATION & RECOVERY**: Because CNG channels close while the $\text{Na}^+/\text{Ca}^{2+},\text{K}^+$ exchanger (NCKX) keeps pumping $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ out, intracellular $[\text{Ca}^{2+}]$ drops from $500\ \text{nM}$ to $50\ \text{nM}$. Low $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ causes **GCAP (Guanylyl Cyclase-Activating Protein)** to stimulate **Guanylyl Cyclase** to resynthesize cGMP, while **Rhodopsin Kinase (GRK1) + Arrestin** turn off $R^*$ and **RGS9** accelerates $G_{t\alpha}$ GTP hydrolysis!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Vision & Sensory Transduction:
• **Summary Flow of Light in a Vertebrate Rod Cell (Memorize Every Arrow!)**:

**Light ($h\nu$) $\rightarrow$ 11-*cis* to All-*trans*-Retinal $\rightarrow$ Metarhodopsin II $\rightarrow$ Active Transducin ($G_{t\alpha}$-GTP) $\rightarrow$ Active cGMP-PDE6 $\rightarrow \downarrow [\text{cGMP}] \rightarrow$ Closure of CNG $\text{Na}^+/\text{Ca}^{2+}$ Channels $\rightarrow$ Membrane HYPERPOLARIZATION ($-40\ \text{mV} \rightarrow -70\ \text{mV}$) $\rightarrow \downarrow$ Presynaptic Glutamate Release!**
• **How do ON-Center vs. OFF-Center Bipolar Cells respond when Light stops Glutamate release?**
– **OFF-Bipolar Cells** express ionotropic **AMPA/Kainate** glutamate receptors (excited by dark glutamate; **hyperpolarized/turned OFF in light**).

– **ON-Bipolar Cells** express the metabotropic receptor **mGluR6** (which in the dark *closes* TRPM1 cation channels; therefore, when light **stops** glutamate release, mGluR6 turns off, TRPM1 opens, and the **ON-Bipolar cell DEPOLARIZES in light**!).

• **Olfactory Sensory Neuron Contrast**: Unlike photoreceptors, Odorant GPCRs ($G_{\text{olf}}$) activate **Adenylyl Cyclase III $\rightarrow \uparrow [\text{cAMP}] \rightarrow$ OPENS CNG $\text{Na}^+/\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels** (followed by $\text{Ca}^{2+}$-activated $\text{Cl}^-$ efflux!), **DEPOLARIZING** the olfactory neuron!
pathology: **Retinitis Pigmentosa** (mutations in Rhodopsin or PDE6$\beta$) & **Leber Congenital Amaurosis (*RPE65* Deficiency)**: *RPE65* is the isomerohydrolase in the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE) that regenerates 11-*cis*-retinal from all-*trans*-retinyl esters; treated with **Luxturna (Voretigene neparvovec)**, the first FDA-approved *in vivo* AAV2 gene therapy!

metrics.sarcomere_bands_contraction: A-Band (Myosin II thick filament length) = CONSTANT! | I-Band (Actin only) & H-Zone (Myosin only) = SHORTEN! | Z-Discs = Move closer!
metrics.giant_rulers: Titin (3.5 MDa elastic spring anchoring Myosin from M-line to Z-disc) & Nebulin (Inelastic ruler specifying exact F-actin thin filament length)
metrics.skeletal_ec_coupling: T-Tubule Cav1.1 (DHPR) physically/mechanically pulls open SR RyR1 (Requires ZERO extracellular Ca2+ influx!)

mechanism: **1. HUXLEY SLIDING FILAMENT GEOMETRY (Z-Disc to Z-Disc $\approx 2.2\ \mu\text{m}$)**:

• **A-Band (Anisotropic / Dark Band)**: Contains the full length of bipolar **Myosin II thick filaments** (plus overlapping thin filaments). **Because neither thick nor thin filaments change their intrinsic length during contraction, the width of the A-Band remains 100% CONSTANT!**

• **I-Band (Isotropic / Light Band)**: Contains **ONLY Actin thin filaments** (plus Titin) flanking the **Z-Disc** (crosslinked by **$\alpha$-Actinin** and capped at the barbed $[+]$ end by **CapZ**, while **Tropomodulin** caps the pointed $[-]$ end). **I-Band SHORTENS** during contraction.
• **H-Zone (Hensen's Zone)**: Central region of the A-band containing **ONLY Myosin thick filaments** bisected by the **M-Line** (Myomesin). **H-Zone SHORTENS** as actin slides inward.
**2. TROPOMYOSIN & THE TROPONIN COMPLEX (TnC, TnI, TnT)**:

In resting muscle (cytosolic $[\text{Ca}^{2+}] < 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$), **Troponin I (TnI, Inhibitory)** holds **Tropomyosin** over the myosin-binding sites on F-actin. When SR $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ release raises cytosolic $[\text{Ca}^{2+}]$ to $10^{-5}\ \text{M}$, binding of **4 $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions to Troponin C (TnC)** causes **Troponin T (TnT)** to roll Tropomyosin deeper into the actin groove—**unmasking the myosin-binding sites** for cross-bridge cycling! Relaxation occurs when the **SERCA pump** pumps $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ back into the Sarcoplasmic Reticulum using ATP.
csir_high_yield: Skeletal vs. Cardiac Excitation–Contraction Coupling (Top CSIR NET Part C Experimental Question!):
• **What happens if a Skeletal Muscle fiber vs. a Cardiac Myocyte is placed in a $\text{Ca}^{2+}$-FREE extracellular Ringer's solution (plus EGTA) and electrically stimulated?**

– **Skeletal Muscle CONTRACTS NORMALLY!** Why? Because at the skeletal muscle **Triad** (1 T-tubule + 2 SR terminal cisternae), the T-tubule voltage sensor **DHPR ($\text{Ca}_v1.1$)** is **physically/mechanically linked** via its II–III cytoplasmic loop directly to the SR **Ryanodine Receptor 1 (RyR1)**! Voltage change alone mechanically pulls RyR1 open without needing any extracellular $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ entry!

– **Cardiac Muscle IMMEDIATELY FAILS TO CONTRACT ('Ringer's Experiment')!** Why? Because at the cardiac **Dyad**, T-tubule **DHPR ($\text{Ca}_v1.2$)** is NOT mechanically connected to **RyR2**! Instead, extracellular $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ MUST enter through $\text{Ca}_v1.2$ during the Phase 2 plateau to bind and open SR **RyR2** (**Calcium-Induced Calcium Release / CICR**)! Furthermore, blocking $\text{Ca}_v1.2$ with **Nifedipine / Verapamil / Diltiazem** inhibits cardiac & smooth muscle contraction while sparing skeletal muscle!
pathology: **Malignant Hyperthermia**: Autosomal dominant mutation in **RYR1** causes volatile anesthetics (Halothane) or succinylcholine to lock SR RyR1 channels open; massive uncontrolled $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ flooding drives relentless ATP consumption, muscle rigidity, and lethal $43^\circ\text{C}$ hyperthermia (treated with the direct RyR1 antagonist **Dantrolene**!).

**Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)**: X-linked frameshift deletions in the giant **Dystrophin** gene (which links cortical F-actin to the sarcolemmal dystroglycan-laminin ECM complex) cause myofiber membrane tearing during contraction.
lab_workbench: Gordon, Huxley & Julian Single-Fiber Length-Tension Curve: Active isometric tension is maximal at a sarcomere length of **$2.0\text{–}2.2\ \mu\text{m}$** (optimal overlap between all myosin cross-bridges and actin); drops linearly to zero at **$3.65\ \mu\text{m}$** (zero overlap between thick and thin filaments!) and drops below $1.65\ \mu\text{m}$ as thin filaments collide across the M-line and thick filaments crumple against the Z-discs.

metrics.no_vasodilation_axis: Endothelial ACh/Shear -> eNOS (L-Arg -> NO gas) -> Smooth Muscle Soluble Guanylyl Cyclase (sGC) -> cGMP -> PKG activates MLCP -> Vasodilation!

mechanism: **1. THICK-FILAMENT (MYOSIN-LINKED) REGULATION IN SMOOTH MUSCLE (vs. Thin-Filament Troponin in Striated Muscle!)**:

• Smooth muscle completely **LACKS Troponin**! Instead, in resting smooth muscle, **Myosin II** is folded into an autoinhibited 10S conformation that cannot interact with actin even though tropomyosin is present.

• **CONTRACTION**: Hormones/neurotransmitters ($G_q \rightarrow \text{IP}_3$) or depolarization (L-type $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels) raise cytosolic $\text{Ca}^{2+}$. Four $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions bind **Calmodulin (CaM)**. The **$\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{–Calmodulin}$ complex** binds and activates **Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK)**, which uses ATP to **phosphorylate Serine-19 on the Myosin Regulatory Light Chain (RLC)**! Only phosphorylated Smooth Muscle Myosin II can unfold, assemble into side-polar filaments, and cycle on actin!

• **RELAXATION & THE LATCH STATE**: **Myosin Light Chain Phosphatase (MLCP)** removes the phosphate from the RLC. *(Note: If RLC is dephosphorylated *while* the myosin head is still attached to actin, detachment slows down dramatically—creating the energy-efficient **'Latch State'** that maintains tonic vascular/sphincter tension for hours while consuming only 1/300th the ATP of skeletal muscle!).*
**2. ENDOTHELIUM-DERIVED NITRIC OXIDE (NO / EDRF) VASODILATION CASCADE (Furchgott, Ignarro & Murad 1998 Nobel Prize)**:

• **Acetylcholine**, Bradykinin, or blood-flow **Shear Stress** on vascular **Endothelial Cells** increases endothelial $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, activating **Endothelial Nitric Oxide Synthase (eNOS)** to convert **L-Arginine + $\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$ L-Citrulline + Nitric Oxide ($\text{NO}$ gas)**.

• Uncharged **$\text{NO}$ gas** diffuses paracrinally into the underlying **Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell** and binds the **Heme moiety of Soluble Guanylyl Cyclase (sGC)**, converting GTP into **cGMP**.

• **cGMP activates Protein Kinase G (PKG)**, which phosphorylates and **activates MLCP** while lowering cytosolic $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ (phosphorylating IRAG/BK channels/PLN) $\rightarrow$ **Smooth Muscle Relaxation & Vasodilation**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Acetylcholine's Intact-Endothelium Paradox & $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ Sensitization:
• **Robert Furchgott's Classic Endothelium-Rubbing Experiment**:

– Adding **Acetylcholine (ACh)** to an arterial ring with an **INTACT Endothelium** causes **VASODILATION** (because ACh binds endothelial $\text{M}_3$ receptors $\rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{eNOS} \rightarrow \text{NO}$ gas diffuses to relax smooth muscle!).

– Adding **Acetylcholine (ACh)** to an arterial ring whose **Endothelium has been gently rubbed off** causes **VASOCONSTRICTION** (because without endothelial NO, ACh acts directly on smooth muscle $\text{M}_3 \rightarrow G_q \rightarrow \text{IP}_3/\text{Ca}^{2+} \rightarrow$ MLCK contraction!).

• **RhoA–ROCK Calcium Sensitization**: Agonists acting through $G_{12/13}$ activate **RhoA $\rightarrow$ Rho-Kinase (ROCK)**, which phosphorylates and **INHIBITS Myosin Light Chain Phosphatase (MLCP)** (via MYPT1/CPI-17)—sustaining strong smooth muscle contraction even when cytosolic $[\text{Ca}^{2+}]$ is low!

• **Nitroglycerin & Sildenafil (Viagra) Synergy**: **Nitroglycerin** is a direct $\text{NO}$ donor (increases cGMP synthesis via sGC); **Sildenafil** inhibits **cGMP-specific Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5)** (blocks cGMP degradation into 5'-GMP). Combining them causes life-threatening hypotensive vasodilation!
pathology: **Asthma Bronchoconstriction vs. $\beta_2$-Agonist Rescue (Salbutamol / Albuterol)**: In bronchial smooth muscle, $\beta_2$-adrenergic agonists activate $G_s \rightarrow \text{Adenylyl Cyclase} \rightarrow \uparrow \text{cAMP} \rightarrow \text{PKA}$. **PKA phosphorylates MLCK**, reducing MLCK's affinity for $\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{–Calmodulin}$ and rapidly relaxing constricted airways!
lab_workbench: Organ-Bath Isometric Aortic Ring Myography with L-NAME: Pre-treating an intact aortic ring with **L-NAME ($N^\omega$-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester**, a competitive inhibitor of NOS) or **ODQ** (oxidizes the sGC heme iron) completely abolishes Acetylcholine-induced relaxation while leaving Sodium Nitroprusside (direct NO donor) relaxation intact (for L-NAME).

agents.name: Tetrodotoxin (TTX — Pufferfish) / Saxitoxin / Lidocaine
agents.binding_site: TTX/STX guanidinium group plugs the EXTRACELLULAR selectivity filter mouth of Nav channels (Lidocaine blocks from the INSIDE!)

resulting_metrics.action_potential_upstroke_mv: -70 mV (0% Action Potential — Complete Conduction Block!)

agents.rescue_experiment: Classic Hodgkin-Huxley Voltage-Clamp Tool: Adding nanomolar TTX to the outside of a squid giant axon completely abolishes the early inward Na+ current while leaving the resting membrane potential (-70 mV) and the delayed outward K+ current 100% intact!

agents.name: Tetraethylammonium (TEA) / 4-Aminopyridine (4-AP)
agents.binding_site: Plugs the delayed-rectifier Kv channel pore, preventing outward K+ repolarization

resulting_metrics.repolarization_duration_ms: 35.0 ms (Massively Prolonged Plateau & Loss of After-Hyperpolarization!)
resulting_metrics.skeletal_twitch_tension: 140% (Prolonged presynaptic Ca2+ entry increases ACh release)

agents.rescue_experiment: With Kv channels blocked by TEA, the rising phase (Na+ influx) is normal, but repolarization now depends solely on slow Na+ h-gate inactivation and leak channels—broadening the action potential 20-fold and abolishing the undershoot!

agents.name: Furosemide (Loop Diuretic)
agents.category: Thick Ascending Limb NKCC2 Cotransporter Blocker
agents.binding_site: Binds the Cl--binding pocket of apical NKCC2 (Na+-K+-2Cl-) in the Thick Ascending Limb of Henle

resulting_metrics.urine_osmolarity_mosm: 300 mOsm/L (Iso-osmotic! Medullary 1,200 mOsm/L Gradient Washed Out!)

agents.rescue_experiment: CSIR Renal Physiology Classic: By shutting down the 'Single Effect' (NKCC2) in the Thick Ascending Limb, Furosemide washes out the entire hypertonic medullary interstitium (dropping it from 1,200 down to 300 mOsm/L). Consequently, the kidney can neither concentrate urine (even if given maximal ADH!) nor dilute urine below 300 mOsm/L!

agents.name: d-Tubocurarine (Curare) / α-Bungarotoxin (Krait Snake Venom)
agents.binding_site: Binds the α-subunit ACh-binding sites on the motor end-plate pentameric Nicotinic Receptor (Curare = reversible competitive; α-Bungarotoxin = quasi-irreversible)
agents.rescue_experiment: Distinguishing Curare from α-Bungarotoxin or Botulinum Toxin: Adding an Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (Neostigmine / Physostigmine) floods the synaptic cleft with endogenous ACh, competitively displacing reversible Curare and restoring muscle twitch tension to 100% (whereas Neostigmine cannot rescue irreversible α-Bungarotoxin!).

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the respiratory node explaining why Fetal Hemoglobin (HbF, α2γ2) has a left-shifted curve (higher O2 affinity) because γ-globin replaces positively charged His-143 with uncharged Serine-143, reducing 2,3-BPG binding.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! In HbF (α2γ2), the γ-chains carry Ser-143 instead of His-143, weakening binding of the T-state stabilizer 2,3-BPG so HbF has higher O2 affinity than maternal HbA.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the renal nephron node where the Thick Ascending Limb ('Diluting Segment') actively pumps out Na+-K+-2Cl- via NKCC2 while remaining 100% impermeable to water, delivering ~100 mOsm/L hypo-osmotic fluid to the DCT.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! The Thick Ascending Limb lacks aquaporins and uses NKCC2 (targeted by Furosemide) to establish the medullary osmotic gradient while diluting the tubular fluid.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the sensory node where light activates Transducin (Gt) and cGMP-Phosphodiesterase (PDE6) to hydrolyze cGMP, CLOSING CNG Na+/Ca2+ channels and HYPERPOLARIZING the cell.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! Vertebrate rods are depolarized in the dark ('Dark Current' via cGMP-gated channels) and hyperpolarize in the light when PDE6 degrades cGMP.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the sarcomere node explaining why skeletal muscle contracts normally in Ca2+-free extracellular solution (mechanical DHPR–RyR1 coupling), whereas cardiac muscle fails immediately (requires Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release via RyR2).
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Skeletal muscle Cav1.1 (DHPR) mechanically pulls open SR RyR1 without needing extracellular Ca2+ entry, whereas cardiac Cav1.2 requires extracellular Ca2+ influx to trigger RyR2.
